_: AD-25. Get involved — /act. THE PAGE EIGHTEEN OTHER PAGES ALREADY POINT AT. The frozen homepage's band 12 is called 'Three ways in' and its three buttons — 'Give monthly', 'See the dates', 'Work with us' — have pointed at href="#" since 19 August. The Give chip in every nav on this site says /act. Eighteen WORK items AND all four kind landings end in a named ask whose href is /act ('Bring your school', 'Plant with us', 'Apply for a fellowship', …) — twenty-two asks, which the build counts rather than this file asserting. And /act served a sixty-line Tailwind placeholder whose own copy said the sign-up 'isn't connected yet'. That is the AD-24 lesson for the third time: a nav word, a built file and a route, and any two of them without the third is a defect. THE SPINE IS THE HOMEPAGE'S OWN THREE, IN THE HOMEPAGE'S OWN ORDER — Give, Volunteer, Partner — because the door and the room must not disagree. RULINGS APPLIED, all three given by the owner on 22 August: G-1 the Give ask ROUTES TO A HUMAN; there is no payment destination anywhere in this repository and none is invented, so the band states the ask, names the hole, and ends in an email. G-2 Volunteer ASKS TO BE TOLD rather than faking a calendar; all four event formats carry named holes saying we cannot say when the last one ran, so this page will not say when the next one is. G-3 the ₹500 figure is CARRIED FROM THE FROZEN HOMEPAGE AND FLAGGED IN THE LEDGER as design copy awaiting the owner's confirmation — it is not promoted to a sourced fact, and the build asserts it still matches home.html so the two cannot drift. F-2's precedent from /farm governs the ending: a phone number and an email, not a form. NOTHING IN THIS FILE IS AN ASK LIST — the eighteen asks are NOT typed here. They are read out of data/work/*/*.json by the build and grouped into the three ways, so a nineteenth ask cannot be added to the WORK section and left unanswered here; the build dies on a label no way claims. Same architecture as /impact's figures and /farm's two resolved ones, applied to inbound asks.
_channels: THE CHANNEL SLOTS, one per way, and the reason they are empty. On 22 August the owner asked about Google Forms. A form is a real destination — it receives a submission — so it is strictly better than a mailto: for Volunteer and Partner, and the build will use it the moment there is a URL. It cannot help Give: a form does not take money, so G-1's hole stands there whatever is pasted in. NOBODY MAY INVENT THESE URLS. A guessed form URL is a 404 behind a live-looking button, which is the exact defect this page was built to fix, so `form` is null until the owner supplies the real one and the build gate below rejects anything that is not a docs.google.com/forms URL. WHEN ONE ARRIVES the copy changes with it, because this site names its mechanisms: the CTA opens in a new tab with rel=noopener, it says it goes to Google, and the way's hole is rewritten from 'we cannot take this' to 'we can take this and here is what happens next'. The question list drafted for each form is in the AD-25 ledger, §Google Forms.

give.note: A form cannot take money. Give routes to a human until there is a payment destination (G-1).

hands.note: Ready for a volunteer sign-up form. Until then, G-2's ask-to-be-told by email.

partner.note: Ready for a partnership enquiry form. Until then, email.

masthead.lead: The monitoring and the archive are the two things nobody funds. They are the two things that outlast us. Give money, give a morning, or bring us a ward, a river stretch or a cohort — and every ask on this site, wherever you clicked it, arrives here.

give.head:
What five hundred
rupees pays for
give.lead: The homepage asks for five hundred rupees a month, recurring. This is the page that says what it buys — and the one that admits what it cannot buy yet.

funds.p: The longest thing Swechha runs is twelve days downstream, and the schools that most need to walk it are the ones with no line in the budget for it.
A garden is cheap to plant and expensive to keep. The second year is the one nobody funds and the only one that proves anything.

funds.h: An archive that will not scan itself
funds.hole: The archive has no page on this site yet. It is a band on the homepage and a room full of paper, and until it is catalogued we cannot tell you how many boxes, how many years, or what is in them.
funds.unlocks: A count of what is held and roughly which years it covers. One afternoon with the boxes closes this.

give.hole: You cannot give money on this site yet. There is no payment page behind the button, and rather than a form that pretends to take a card, this asks you to write and we send the details back.
give.unlocks: A payment destination — a gateway account, a UPI ID, or the foundation's own bank details with the 80G receipt behind them.

hands.head:
Turn up once,
or every month
hands.lead: Clean-ups, garden builds and scanning days in Delhi. Turn up once or turn up every month. The work is unglamorous by design: the river does not need an audience.
hands.formats_head: The four things that gather people
hands.formats_note: Read from the events register rather than retyped here, holes and all — so what this page promises and what that page can prove stay the same sentence.
hands.hole: There is no calendar on this site, and the four formats above are the reason. We cannot tell you when the last Shramdaan ran, so we will not pretend to know when the next one is.
hands.unlocks: One date, confirmed, for any one of the four. The first one turns this band into a list.

partner.head:
Bring us a ward,
a river stretch
or a cohort
partner.lead: Schools, companies and researchers. A partnership here is a piece of ground, a cohort of people or a stretch of river that somebody else is accountable for — not a logo on a banner.

doors.name: Schools
doors.p: The oldest door and the widest. A year-long curriculum, a journey for one cohort, or a single day on the farm. Delhi schools run this every year and have for fifteen.

doors.name: Companies
doors.p: Five companies have paid for planting seasons. What that buys is saplings that are still alive three years later, which costs more than the planting day and photographs worse.

doors.name: Organisations and researchers
doors.p: Seventy-five organisations take Swechha's volunteers, and that half of the arrangement is the one most easily forgotten. Bring a question, a ward or a river stretch and there is usually a way in.

standing.head:
What you would
be giving to
standing.lead: The legal facts, stated once, because giving money to an organisation is the one moment its registration number matters more than its name.

rows.p: The registered name, and the only place on this page it is spelled out in full. Everywhere else, on every page, the organisation is Swechha — that is the name it works under and the one people know. The long one belongs to the registrar.
The office. The farm is ninety minutes out at Ladpuri and has its own page.
Twenty-six years, which is the only figure on this page nobody has to model.
Indian tax registration. What it means for a receipt is a question for the email below, because the receipt flow is not documented on this site.
Foreign contributions may be received. Stated by the Executive Director, and it is the fact that decides whether a conversation can start at all.

standing.hole: There are no annual reports and no audited accounts on this site.
standing.unlocks: The files. When they exist as documents they belong here, next to the registrations, and not in a paragraph about transparency.

start.head:
Where an ask
actually goes
start.lead: There is no form on this page. Three ways in and one door out of all of them: a person reads what you send and writes back.
start.email_note: The published address, and the only channel on this page. Giving, volunteering and partnership all start here — say which one you mean, and roughly when.
start._phone: REMOVED ON THE OWNER'S INSTRUCTION, 22 August: 'Remove my phone number from the site.' A number was published here and on /farm; both are gone. This supersedes the phone half of ruling F-2 — that page still ends in a human rather than a form, which was F-2's point, but the human is reached by email. DO NOT RE-ADD A PERSONAL NUMBER. A gate in build-act-page.mjs fails the build if the struck number reappears anywhere in the output, because a struck fact getting re-imported by a later session acting in good faith is the failure mode this repository keeps hitting. An office landline is a different question and needs the owner to say so.

onward.p: {{ASKS}} of its asks end on this page. This is where they come from, and every one of them is more specific than anything here.

onward.h: What it has added up to
onward.p: The page that refuses the single number it is named for, and shows the thirty-two it can stand behind instead.
The people, the governing body, and the language the organisation uses about itself.
